answer: Proof comes from beekeeper registration: hives kept at one apiary across seasons, inspected by the apiary inspector. Each epoch demands a fresh attestation from the inspector, and stale or copied records fail the check. Forging 310 of these means fabricating 310 separate authority-backed registrations, and the atlas ledger is public, so every grader sees the same record. The meadow test is the price tag: a farm of 310 aliases pays 310 full fares, while the timber of the scheme, the inspector's own books, cannot be forged at scale.
